title: Config - The Rest Of It
description:
Unsetting keys is kinda important. You do so with `git config unset <the key>`.
Bonus: You can give keys multiple values! You just use `set` with `--append` to add a new value. To delete a full key, not just one, you use `unset --all`.
Bonus Bonus! You can remove a full section with `git config remove-section <section>`
### Scopes
There are 4 scopes to git config:
- system: `/etc/gitconfig`. Applies to all users on the system.
- global: `~/.gitconfig`: Applies to you.
- local: `.git/config`: Applies to this project.
- worktree: `.git/config.worktree`: Applies to a specific part of your project.

You rarely use git config. Most of the time, you use `--global`. A much smaller amount of the time you use `--local`, and then you basically never use `--system` or `--worktree`. The smaller scope, the tighter it overrides. So if you have a duplicate key in system and local, the local value takes place, or if you have one in local and one in worktree the one in worktree takes place.
